history.summary: CSV CORRECTION: 'Pancha Ratna Temple, Bishnupur, Manipur' is documented as the Pancha Ratna (Shyam Rai) Temple at Bishnupur, BANKURA district, WEST BENGAL - the CSV's state (Manipur) is wrong; the town name Bishnupur exists in both states and this conflation (also seen on aggregator sites that label the Bankura temple 'Bishnupur, Manipur') is common. DUPLICATE CROSS-REF: 'Pancha Ratna Temple' is the widely used alternate name of the Shyam Rai Temple documented as seq 648 in this batch - the two CSV rows describe the SAME monument; consider merging or removing one. The temple was built in 1643 AD by Malla King Raghunath Singha (son of Bir Hambir/Dhir Hambir). It is the finest surviving example of the Pancha-ratna (five-spired) style of Bengal: brick-built on a low square plinth with an ambulatory pathway and a three-arched porch on each side; the central shikhara is octagonal while the other four are square. The walls are richly decorated with terracotta carvings depicting Krishna-lila (including the Raslila), the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and scenes of contemporary social life. Maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India; one of the most visited monuments of the Bishnupur temple town.

name: Pancha Ratna Temple
town_description: Bishnupur in Bankura district, West Bengal, was the capital of the Malla dynasty from the 8th century and is famous as Bengal's terracotta temple town - Rasmancha (c.1600), Jor Bangla (1655), Shyam Rai/Pancharatna (1643), Madan Mohan and others. The town is also home to the Bishnupur Gharana of Hindustani classical music, Baluchari silk weaving, and the famous Bankura terracotta horse. Not to be confused with Bishnupur, Manipur.
tradition: Vaishnavism (Gaudiya Vaishnavism, rooted in the teachings of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, which the Malla kings embraced in the 16th century; dedicated to Radha-Krishna)
